post.title: The Worst Scorers Thought They Were Above Average #shorts
post.description: Quiz night: Otto is sure he crushed it, Arthur is sure he bombed, and the scores say the opposite. In Kruger & Dunning's 1999 paper "Unskilled and Unaware of It" (Journal of Personality and Social Psychology), four studies tested humour, logical reasoning and English grammar; people in the bottom quarter averaged around the 12th percentile but estimated themselves around the 62nd. Their explanation: the skill you need to get answers right is the same skill you need to judge whether they're right. Honest caveat: later work (Krueger & Mueller 2002, and statistical analyses in 2022) showed part of the pattern can come from statistics (regression to the mean) and a general better-than-average bias, while a large 2021 replication still found low performers were worse at judging whether their own answers were right. Everyone's a beginner at something. #psychology #shorts #dunningkruger
